course_name_original: Religions of the World: Humans and the Sacred
course_name_en: Religions of the World: Humans and the Sacred
prerequisites: General historical and humanistic knowledge expected from a high school graduate, including basic information on the major religions of the world (especially Christianity and Judaism).

learning_outcomes.text: The student has general knowledge about the origin, history, and internal structure of the main religions of the world.
The student has more detailed knowledge about the history and characteristics of various branches of Christianity.
The student can distinguish and analyze the characteristics of the great religious and spiritual traditions of the world.
The student can independently undertake and solve theoretical and practical problems of spirituality, religious culture, and the interface between religion and science.
The student can differentiate religious, cultural, and spiritual traditions characteristic of the main branches of Christianity.
The student understands the essence of human rights and adopts an attitude consistent with their idea regarding the presence of religion in society and culture.
The student can develop their own open and critical attitude towards various religious and spiritual traditions shaped within and beyond the great religions of the world.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Introduction to basic concepts and issues: Concept of religion, sacrum and spirituality and their mutual relations. Common and scientific typologies of religions. Religions vs. religious studies and philosophy of religion. Outline of the history and geography of the great religions of the world.

Religions of the West, their mutual connections and evolution: Origin of Jewish monotheism. Ancient and modern Judaism - religion of the Covenant and the Law. Jewish roots of Christianity and contemporary relations between these religions. Origin and specificity of Muslim monotheism and its connections with Jewish and Christian monotheism. Outline of the history of Islam, contemporary Islam.

Origin, development and contemporaneity of Christianity: Early Christianity between the Jewish and Greek worlds. Formation of the doctrinal foundations of Christianity. Orthodox monastic-mystical tradition; icon - a window to heaven - a lens of Orthodox religiosity. Petrine primacy as the basis of Catholic religious identity. Reformation, sola fide and sola scriptura, socio-economic significance of Protestant ethics.

Religions of the Middle East: The oldest roots of Indian religions. Basic concepts of Hinduism, Brahmanic religiosity. Development of Hinduism - period of meditation, Jainism, sources of Buddhism. Mission of Gautama Shakyamuni - Buddha. Basic concepts and principles of Buddhism. Mahayana, Theravada and Vajrayana Buddhism. Ethical-spiritual model of arhat and bodhisattva. Contemporary Buddhism in the Western world and in Poland.

Religions of the Far East: Taoism and Confucianism. Traditional Chinese identity - synthesis of Taoism, Confucianism and Buddhism. Foundations of Confucian ethics, its economic and social significance. Confucianism and contemporary Far East. Shintoism - traditional national and state religion of the Japanese. Genesis of Shintoism, its place in the cultural and spiritual landscape of the Far East.

assessment_methods.method: Preparation of an essay on a selected topic

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by passing a written final test, with the possibility of supplementation or oral correction. Active participation in lectures (discussion) and/or preparation of an essay on a selected topic can increase the grade by one level. The final grade is calculated according to the university's rules defining the relationship between the percentage of mastered material and the grade, taking into account the possibility of grade increase.
